name: statesmith
desc: State machine code generation tool suitable for bare metal, embedded and more
why: Generates embedded state machine code from diagrams, a niche code-generation idea that rewards a long look.

brief.what_it_is: StateSmith is a free, open source, cross-platform tool that generates state machine code in several programming languages from a diagram. The README describes the output as human readable with zero dependencies, and says it avoids dynamic memory allocation. The tutorials use PlantUML or draw.io diagrams as input and run through the ss.cli command line tool. The generated code is meant for targets from tiny bare-metal microcontrollers to games, apps and web. The languages named in the tutorial are C, C++, C#, JavaScript, Java and Python.
brief.why_it_exists: The author says he could not find a quality state machine code generator that met his needs, had an attractive license, and was enjoyable to use. He also wants the diagram to stay accurate, so that code is generated from the documentation instead of being hand-synced with a drawing.
brief.how_it_works: You draw a state machine in a supported diagram tool, then run the ss.cli tool to generate code from that diagram. The tutorials say the spec integration tests read a diagram file, generate code, compile and run it in another process, and check the resulting behavior. The README does not describe the internal generation pipeline beyond that.

Wiki install method using the dotnet SDK (6, 7 or 8); puts ss.cli on the PATH so it runs from any directory.

brief.install_notes: Two routes. The dotnet route needs the .NET SDK 6, 7 or 8 and the command dotnet tool install --global StateSmith.Cli; the wiki says it is the smallest and fastest install at about 28 MB. The standalone route needs no dotnet: download the prebuilt binary from the GitHub releases page (the wiki links cli-v0.19.0) and extract ss.cli, or ss.cli.exe on Windows. Linux and macOS builds are about 50 MB each, with Alpine and ARM Linux builds also offered. The wiki says arm64 macOS was not working and recommends the x64 build, which runs on Apple silicon. No account is needed. I did not see a Homebrew-specific section, so the brew formula's ss.cli executable is the only evidence I have that it installs that way.
brief.standout: Instead of writing a state machine by hand and drawing it separately, you draw it once and generate the code from the diagram, with tests that check the generated behavior by compiling and running it. The author also says the design avoids dynamic allocation and dependencies, which suits bare-metal work.
brief.status: Appears maintained, though the evidence is thin. The wiki install page was last edited Sep 20, 2025 and references CLI release cli-v0.19.0. The README reports more than 730 tests and says the author's company uses it in production. I did not see commit dates or a release date, so I cannot confirm the cadence.
brief.caveats: The wiki says macOS testing is limited and arm64 binaries were not working when written. The README says adding new languages is tricky and that the author hopes for contributors. The README calls the project free and open source but I did not see a license name, so check the repository before depending on it. The tutorials are built around PlantUML and draw.io, and I did not see other diagram inputs. The standalone binaries are about 50 MB.
quotes: StateSmith is a cross platform, free/open source tool for generating state machines in multiple programming languages.
It avoids dynamic memory allocations for the safety or performance inclined.
I couldn't find a quality state machine code generator that met my needs, had an attractive license, and was enjoyable to use.
